reason: The cited evidence does not directly address the effect of particle size on deposition efficiency, thickness, or oxidation for FeCoNiCrAl. E1 discusses phase changes and oxidation in thermal-sprayed HEAs but does not link particle size to thickness or oxidation reduction. E2 describes splat morphology for a different HEA using a specific milled powder but provides no comparison of particle size effects on thickness or oxidation. The key premises thus lack specific prior support.
premises: Larger feedstock particles increase deposition efficiency and coating thickness
Coarser particles have higher thermal inertia, melt more fully, and flatten better
Larger particles have lower surface area-to-volume ratio, reducing in-flight oxidation
Improved splat flattening and interlamellar bonding yield a thicker, adherent coating
Phase makeup and oxidation levels will be comparable or improved relative to the fine-powder baseline
